newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil leader wanted no role in Falklands - report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil leader wanted no role in Falklands - report.

text.p: Brazil's then-President Joao Figuereido refused to take phone calls from Argentine dictator Leopoldo Galtieri in the weeks before the 1982 Falklands War for fear of being dragged into a conflict with Britain, a newsweekly said on Sunday.

News magazine Veja quoted Octavio Aguiar de Medeiros, the former head of the Brazilian intelligence agency, as saying Figuereido was afraid Galtieri would ask Brazil for arms needed to fight the British.

According to Medeiros, Figuereido said: "Galtieri has already called home twice. He wants to speak to me. It can only be regarding the Malvinas issue and I don't want to get involved in this because he's going to want to pressure me.
"I don't know what to do because I don't want to talk to him, not even over the phone."

The Malvinas is the name Argentina uses for the South Atlantic archipielago over which it fought a brief but bloody 10-week war with Britain that began on April 2, 1982. More than 1,000 soldiers, mostly Argentine, were killed in the conflict, which triggered the collapse of the military junta after Argentine armed forces were defeated in battle.
Figuereido was Brazil's last military dictator during 21 years of military rule.

Veja said Medeiros volunteered to travel to Buenos Aires to meet with Galtieri before the war began, a proposal that Figuereido approved. In a midnight meeting at the Casa Rosada, the Argentine presidential palace, Medeiros said, Galtieri was expansive, saying Britain had usurped the Falklands.
"We will defeat them. We will never raise the white flag. Never. Never," Medeiros quoted Galtieri as saying.

He said Galtieri did not ask for Brazilian weapons at the time but an Argentine request for help was made near the end of the war. He said Brazil finally loaned Argentina a dozen outdated Xavante fighter jets and did not bill the Argentines since the jets were already set to be retired.
